analysis: The broad plan illustrates the generic degree through all six clusters. Development, rhetoric, programming and sustainability in the first semester are followed by brain and behaviour, quantitative and qualitative methods, data and political and media studies. It applies these skills in governance, cognition, econometrics, historical research and documentary analysis. The business example develops from product design, venture foundations, economics and accounting into the management and analysis of ventures and markets. Its AI business course concerns organisational and policy consequences. Its later courses add customer research, economic policy, finance, negotiation, marketing and econometrics. The data example develops from programming, data analysis, logic and calculus through algorithms, matrix methods, probability and machine learning to robotics, optimisation, reinforcement learning and neural networks. Software, networks and data management support implementation, and ethics, experimental methods and persuasion support responsible design and communication. Description-only courses were assessed as substantive where their descriptions support the role, including strategy and digital transformation, historical research, econometrics, market research, databases and reinforcement learning. The mandatory development course aligns directly across all columns. Advanced and other course choice are allocations of credits with many qualifying courses, so they are shown separately rather than paired with any single UCR course. The remaining four official clusters each support a credible direction. The existing pair of business and data is retained under the three-example ceiling as the next two official clusters in order, with distinct coherent course sequences.
